correctness.rationale: Every semigroup element has a unique expression j b + k a with 0≤j<a and k≥0; subtracting the resulting Hilbert series from 1/(1−z) gives the gap polynomial. At a nonidentity m-root only one generator factor can vanish. Cancelling 1−z^a when z^a=1 gives b/(1−z^b), with the symmetric limit at z^b=1. A legal b-step changes only the mean and the modes in the nonidentity d-root subgroup, there by −m/(1−z^b). In the sawtooth inversion sum S_j=Σ_{w^d=1,w≠1} w^(−j)/(1−w), conjugate pairing gives S_0=(d−1)/2, and S_j−S_(j−1)=−1 for 1≤j<d; relabel w=z^b. The genus change then gives the claimed shift. For integrality, a and d have the same parity: if a is even both b and b+m must be odd for a legal shift, so d is even. The symmetric step is identical upon exchange. In the full decomposition, divisibility subgroups are disjoint away from 1 and the residual depends only on a,b modulo m. Each nonzero root denominator has modulus at least 4/m, and each two-factor numerator at most 2. Thus |R(r)|≤m/4+m²/8. CRT realizes both simultaneous extremes of the two independent centered residues; the oscillation of the residual bounds the error in their range. When m divides a and b≡1, every nonidentity Fourier mode reduces to (1−b)/(1−z), which inverts to the claimed exact histogram. The progressions concern admissible pairs, not walks through noncoprime intermediates.

value.rationale: For a natural gap distribution, nonunit moduli need not just spoil exact balance: each resonant generator contributes its own independent linear slope to the maximum imbalance, uniformly over unrestricted generator sizes. This separates two arithmetic sources of bias and predicts legal changes without recomputing gaps; the divisibility histogram gives an exact boundary case. A sharper bound in the unit case is already available and is not the reason for the value finding.
residual_risks: The bound need not be optimal, and no analogous error theorem is established for more generators.
